evidence: Six research shards (207 lineups, positions 1 to 207 of LINEUPS in src/lib/missingXi.ts) read on 2026-10-05 from the organiser's match data (UEFA, fifa.com, Premier League, LaLiga, bundesliga.com, CONMEBOL pages) and an independent report (ESPN, Sky Sports, BeSoccer, RSSSF and others), each re-checked by a skeptic on other hosts. No wiki was used. Round 1026 re-read ESPN's summary feed, UEFA's lineup feed, the fifa.com live feed and a few squad lists on 2026-10-06 where a decision needed it; those reads are named in the row that used them.
files: shard-1.json to shard-6.json, one row per lineup in LINEUPS order. Each row: position, id, research verdict, verdict (verified, corrected, noted, held), eleven (the starters both XI hosts publish), aka (entry spelling to published spelling where the accent fold does not match), substitutes, fields and hints (the entry's values after this round), sources (host, url, readOn, xi, says), diffs (each research diff with its decision and reason), applied (path, from, to, why) and notes.
rules: 1. A field changes only when two independent non-wiki sources agree on the new value and no skeptic contradicted it. Where sources split the entry keeps its value and the row records the split.
2. Priority is what a player sees: the hint fields on blanks (club at the time, position label, nationality), then the starting eleven, then score, date and venue, then formation labels.

3. A skeptic's missed diff is a lead. It is applied only when this round read it on two hosts itself and no host contradicts it; otherwise it is a note. (The first fold applied three leads on one own read; the review fix gave each a second own read or withdrew it: see seriea-2019-juve-title, cl-2010-semi-inter, bundesliga-2020-bayern-title.)
4. A venue renamed since (Millennium Stadium and Principality Stadium) is the same ground; that is a note, not a correction.
5. A nationality hint follows the senior national team the man played for, not a passport line in a feed.

6. A lineup the research could not put on two hosts is kept only if its eleven matches a reachable source and nothing contradicts it; otherwise it is held (verdict held, with the reason, the measured cost of removing it from the daily rotation and a rebuild proposal) and the entry is not changed.
conventions: Eleven: every row's eleven is vouched for by at least two distinct hosts whose source carries xi true. bundesliga-2018-bayern-title, which first rested on ESPN plus a partial bundesliga.com read, now has Sky (sport.sky.de) and Fox Sports as full hosts, and the harness carries no exemption.
Names: the entry and the published eleven match when normalizeName (the game's own fold) agrees, after a German oe, ue, ae fold and a word-order fold, or through the row's explicit aka.

Wrong starter: the man the two hosts list takes the slot of the man who did not start, and never inherits that man's role. His tile shows, in this order: the role two hosts state for this match; otherwise the role one match source states (ESPN's formation feed, UEFA or fifa.com pitch coordinates, a line by line team sheet under a formation, a match report sentence) when no host contradicts it, marked open in the row; otherwise the line his hosts' position listings give, written DF, MF or FW. A position listing (UEFA fieldPosition, fifa.com Position, ESPN D/M/F, a feed's grouping) is the man's registered line, so it never outranks a match source. One replacement (Salihamidzic, cl-2001-final-bayern) has no host stating anything and keeps the slot label, recorded as open.

Formation: changes when two hosts agree on the shape, counting an organiser's pitch coordinates as a statement of shape. When the hosts agree only on the lines (one states 4-1-4-1, the other four defenders, five midfielders and one forward), the label is the lines both state (4-5-1). When the old label is refuted but the hosts state different shapes, or only one host states any, the label is left empty and the page shows none: keeping a refuted label would show something false and choosing one host would pick a side. Six rows: cl-2007-final-milan, cl-2017-r16-barca, cl-2017-semi-monaco and wc-2018-semi-belgium show none; euro-2008-final-spain and cl-2005-semi-liverpool show 4-5-1. This empty label is a reading of rule 1 the lead has to ratify.

Sides: a tile moves left or right only when two hosts agree on the side. A line by line team sheet printed in a fixed order under a formation (goal.com, Sky, an Italian tabellino, bundesliga.com) counts as stating the side when its order matches an explicit host on the full-backs; where two such sheets order a line differently (the Juventus centre-backs in 2020) it is a split. A tile centred because a two host shape leaves it alone in its line (a lone striker, the middle of a back three) needs no side source. A tile that has to move because a replacement takes the side the one host states for him, or because a two host shape change puts two men side by side, moves with its why marked 'Forced, not chosen'. A move on one host with no such reason is withdrawn (libertadores-2018-final-river).

Blanks: a candidate who did not start is dropped. A lineup left with fewer than two gets a replacement who started on both hosts, spelled as an earlier verified blank where possible; on national-team lineups a new blank's club comes from two squad lists. Every starter is offered to the guess box through XI_ROSTER_NAMES, and simMissingXiReach (live, run by the lead at release) sweeps every blank against player_market_values.
Facts: a reveal-screen fact that the hosts contradict is removed, never rewritten from memory. The filler 'Started that night for <club>' is false on national-team lineups and was removed there.
Comments and the internal source field: where they vouched for the wrong eleven, score or venue they now say what changed and point here.
